title: 9 Best Trust Accounting Software for Vacation Rental Managers
summary: Compare 9 trust accounting options for vacation rental managers, from Topkey and VRPlatform to Track, Escapia, Guesty Accounting and spreadsheets.
body_markdown:
*Updated November 2026*


Whose money is in your trust account right now?


An owner can ask. So can an auditor or a state regulator. They'll want it broken down by owner, guest deposit and tax, down to the penny. Most vacation rental managers can answer at month-end, after a long reconciliation. Few can answer on a random Tuesday.


Good trust accounting software makes that answer available any day. This guide compares nine options: standalone trust accounting tools, trust accounting built into a PMS, and the spreadsheet workaround many teams still use. Topkey is first, and the rest follow in reading order.


## The 9 Options at a Glance


Option Type Best for


Topkey Standalone, works with your PMS and ledger Daily trust reconciliation without switching PMS


VRPlatform Standalone STR ledger One STR ledger for trust and company books


Track Inside a PMS Track users with a trust accountant on staff


Escapia Inside a PMS Large managers who want an all-in-one system


Streamline Inside a PMS Streamline users


Guesty Accounting Inside a PMS Guesty users


Hospitable Inside a PMS Eligible Hospitable users


CiiRUS Inside a PMS CiiRUS users who want a general ledger built in


Spreadsheets and QuickBooks Manual workaround Small portfolios with simple owner setups


## How We Picked and Checked These Tools


Every option here keeps owner and guest money separate from company money and is used by vacation rental managers. We also included the spreadsheet workaround, because it's what many teams run today.


We checked each tool's trust accounting features on its own website on November 24 and 25, 2026. We left out pricing because it changes often. Nothing here is legal advice, so confirm your state's trust accounting rules with your accountant.


## What Good Trust Accounting Software Does


It keeps a separate ledger for each kind of money you hold. Owner funds, guest deposits, taxes and your own management fees all sit in the same bank account. The software keeps them apart on paper, so no one's money pays someone else's bill.


It also runs three-way reconciliation. That means the bank statement, the trust ledger and the total of every owner's balance all have to agree. If one is off, you know there's a problem before an owner or auditor finds it.


And it breaks lump-sum payouts back into reservations. One Airbnb or Vrbo deposit can cover a dozen stays. Until it's split, you can't say which owner it belongs to.


Rules differ by state, and some states regulate vacation rental trust accounts closely. Check your state's requirements with your accountant.


## Standalone Trust Accounting


These two run trust accounting outside your PMS. Topkey works alongside the PMS and general ledger you already have. VRPlatform becomes your general ledger.


### 1. Topkey


Topkey is the AI-powered financial operating system built specifically for vacation rental managers. Its trust accounting keeps owner, guest and company money apart and reconciled every day, alongside the PMS you already run.


**How it handles trust accounting.**[Topkey's trust accounting](https://topkey.io/trust-accounting) keeps a double-entry ledger by account and month, with owner money, guest deposits, manager money and taxes kept apart across one or more trust bank accounts.


Each day it matches OTA and processor payouts to deposits and reservations. Airbnb connects directly, Vrbo, Booking.com and Marriott match from their reports, and underpaid or unmatched payouts get flagged mid-month instead of at close.


A period only closes once those checks pass, and owner statements are checked against the ledger before you finalize them and pay owners in bulk. It works with Guesty, Track, Hostaway and Hostfully, even alongside PMS trust accounting.


Setup is careful, too. Topkey checks your opening bank, owner and tax balances against the bank before go-live, then carries owner balances forward each period. Because expenses, bills and[revenue reconciliation](https://topkey.io/revenue-reconciliation) run in the same system, money moving in and out of trust is already tagged to the right property and owner.


**Where Topkey isn't the right fit.** If you only manage properties you own, you're not holding anyone else's money, so you likely don't need trust accounting. Topkey isn't a general ledger either, so your company books stay in QuickBooks, Xero or similar.


**Best for:** managers on Guesty, Track, Hostaway or Hostfully who want trust accounting reconciled daily, not monthly. Smaller teams get it without a PMS switch, and larger groups run it beside their PMS trust accounting as a daily check.


[Visit Topkey](https://topkey.io/trust-accounting)


### 2. VRPlatform (VRTrust)


VRTrust is VRPlatform's trust accounting software, built by short-term rental accountants.


**What it does well.** VRTrust is a full general ledger that supports trust reconciliation. It runs three-way reconciliation between the bank ledger balance, bank statements and owner balances, and tracks guest, owner, tax and deposit balances. Owner and operating funds stay separate inside one system, batch deposits break out to reservations, and owners can be paid by ACH.


**Where it falls short.** Because VRTrust is your general ledger, adopting it means moving your company books too. That's a bigger decision than adding trust accounting, and your CPA will want a say.


**Best for:** managers who want trust and company books in one STR-specific ledger.


[Visit VRPlatform](https://www.vrplatform.app/features/trust-accounting-software-property-managers)


## Trust Accounting Inside a PMS


These options come with a property management system. So the first question isn't how good the trust accounting is. It's whether you'd run that PMS anyway.


### 3. Track


Track is an enterprise vacation rental PMS whose customers often pick it for the trust accounting alone.


**What it does well.** For trust work, Track is about as deep as PMS accounting gets. Its ledger-based system has been around for roughly 20 years and covers the hard cases, like owner taxes and IRS withholding on foreign owners' earnings, backed by more than 60 accounting and owner reports.


**Where it falls short.** It's only on Track, and Track says it's made by and for trust accountants. Teams without that expertise in-house have a lot to learn.


**Best for:** Track users with a trust accountant on staff.


[Visit Track](https://trackhospitality.com/features/vacation-rental-trust-accounting-software/)


### 4. Escapia


Escapia, owned by Expedia Group, has been doing vacation rental trust accounting for more than 25 years.


**What it does well.** Escapia markets its trust accounting as "to-the-penny accurate," and large managers have leaned on it for years. Because it's part of the PMS, reservations land in the trust ledger without a sync in between.


**Where it falls short.** You adopt Escapia's whole platform to get it. If your team likes its current PMS, that's a lot to change for accounting.


**Best for:** large managers who want reservations and trust accounting in one system.


[Visit Escapia](https://escapia.com/features/trust-accounting/)


### 5. Streamline


Streamline is an enterprise PMS with an NC-accredited trust accounting suite.


**What it does well.** Streamline built its accounting to fit the trust accounting practices you already follow. You can pay vendors in trust or out of trust, and track travel agent income and expenses.


**Where it falls short.** It's part of the Streamline platform, so it only fits if Streamline runs your reservations.


**Best for:** Streamline users, especially those in North Carolina.


[Visit Streamline](https://www.streamlinevrs.com/features/trust-accounting/)


### 6. Guesty Accounting


Guesty's accounting module is built into the Guesty PMS.


**What it does well.** Guesty's accounting starts from the assumption that guest money lands in a trust account. Airbnb payouts, which arrive as a jumble of payments and adjustments, get grouped automatically, and AI suggests bank matches. For regulated markets, Guesty says it meets North Carolina and Queensland trust accounting rules.


**Where it falls short.** It's only for Guesty users. If you leave Guesty, you leave your trust accounting setup behind.


**Best for:** Guesty users who want trust accounting in their PMS.


[Visit Guesty Accounting](https://www.guesty.com/features/accounting/)


### 7. Hospitable


Hospitable offers trust accounting to eligible property managers on its platform.


**What it does well.** It syncs your trust account's bank feed and suggests matches from the owner statements you already publish in Hospitable. Deposits, owner payouts and management fee transfers get recorded with context. Owner-level ledgers and reports stay audit-ready.


**Where it falls short.** It's only for eligible managers, so confirm before you plan around it. It's also built on Hospitable's own owner statements.


**Best for:** eligible Hospitable users.


[Visit Hospitable](https://hospitable.com/features/trust-accounting)


### 8. CiiRUS


CiiRUS is a vacation rental PMS with trust accounting built in.


**What it does well.** Alongside trust accounting, CiiRUS includes owner statements, escrow tracking, vendor bills, ACH disbursements, 1099 prep and a full general ledger. That's a lot of accounting inside one PMS.


**Where it falls short.** Because the general ledger lives inside the PMS, adopting CiiRUS usually means moving your reservations and your company books at the same time. That's two big changes in one project.


**Best for:** CiiRUS users who want a general ledger inside their PMS.


[Visit CiiRUS](https://ciirus.com/platform/trust-accounting)


## The Manual Workaround


### 9. Spreadsheets and QuickBooks


Many teams start with a spreadsheet of owner balances sitting next to QuickBooks.


**What it does well.** It's familiar, flexible and needs nothing new. For a handful of owners with simple contracts, it can work.


**Where it falls short.** QuickBooks has no owner ledger, so the spreadsheet carries the most important numbers you have. Reconciliation is manual. And one broken formula can hide a shortfall for months, until an owner or auditor finds it.


**Best for:** small portfolios with simple owner setups.


## The Bottom Line


If your PMS already has strong trust accounting, use it. Topkey can run alongside it for daily reconciliation and the expense side. If your PMS doesn't have trust accounting, Topkey adds it without a PMS switch.


[See Topkey's trust accounting](https://topkey.io/trust-accounting)


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is trust accounting in vacation rental management?


Trust accounting is how vacation rental managers track money they hold for others, such as owner funds, guest deposits and taxes, separately from the company's own money. Each owner and each kind of money gets its own ledger, and those ledgers are reconciled against the bank.


### Do vacation rental managers need trust accounting?


If you hold owner or guest money, you need to keep it separate, and many states require trust accounting for vacation rental managers. Rules vary, so check your state's requirements with your accountant.


### Can QuickBooks do trust accounting?


Not on its own. QuickBooks has no built-in owner ledgers or trust reconciliation, so managers who use it for trust money usually keep owner balances in spreadsheets. Most pair QuickBooks with PMS trust accounting or a tool like Topkey.


### What is three-way reconciliation?


Three-way reconciliation checks that three numbers agree: the trust bank statement, the trust ledger and the total of all owner balances. If any one is off, there's an error to find.


### Do I need a new PMS to get trust accounting?


No. Topkey runs trust accounting alongside Guesty, Track, Hostaway and Hostfully, and VRPlatform connects to several PMSs. PMS-built options like Track, Escapia, Streamline, Guesty Accounting, Hospitable and CiiRUS come with their own PMS.


### How often should a trust account be reconciled?


Most managers reconcile at least monthly, and some states set their own schedule. Software like Topkey reconciles payouts against deposits and reservations every day, so problems surface during the month instead of at close.
